claims.claim: Palette is a small appellation in Provence, a few kilometers east of Aix-en-Provence.
The appellation covers about 50 hectares, strictly delimited.
French Wikipedia gives 52 hectares planted in 2024: 25 red, 19 white, 8 rosé.
claims.note: Single secondary source, read through a summary.

claims.claim: The vines grow in Aix-en-Provence, Meyreuil and Le Tholonet. The hamlet of Palette lies in Le Tholonet.
The AOC Palette was classified by decree on 28 April 1948. It extended the earlier recognition of Château Simone, obtained by Jean Rougier in 1946.
claims.note: Producer's account. The 1946 date conflicts between the two producer pages (see conflicts).

claims.claim: Soils are scree (éboulis) from limestone, on the calcaires de Langesse.
Soils are thin, stony and skeletal, on Lutetian Tertiary limestones, including lake limestones.
claims.quote: sols squelettiques de peu d'épaisseur et caillouteux

claims.claim: Vines sit mostly on hillsides facing Mont Sainte-Victoire.
The site is a wooded bowl, sheltered from the wind by nearby heights.
White Palette is at least 80% Clairette. Bourboulenc, Trebbiano, Grenache blanc and Muscat varieties may make up the rest.
Red and rosé Palette is at least 80% Grenache, Mourvèdre and Cinsault.
Yields are capped at 40 hl/ha. Wines must reach at least 11% alcohol.
Harvest is by hand, and winemaking must happen inside the delimited area.
Producers include Château Simone, Château Crémade and Château Henri Bonnaud. Château de Meyreuil and Château des Trois Sautets are also listed.
Château Simone is the best-known Palette estate.
claims.note: Common view, but no source here gives Simone's share of the appellation. Do not state a share or say it dominates without one.

conflicts: Château Simone's own pages date the 'Château Simone' recognition 21 July 1946 (AOC page) and 21 February 1946 (family page).

White grape rules: English Wikipedia says at least 80% Clairette. French Wikipedia says the main grapes (araignan, bourboulenc, clairette, clairette rose) must make at least 55%. The producer lists Clairette, Grenache blanc and Bourboulenc as the whites.
Size: about 50 ha (producer) against 52 ha planted in 2024 (French Wikipedia).
gaps: Château Simone's share of Palette's vineyard or output. Not found, so 'dominates' is unproven.
